output.brief: Don't roll back the gateway. The latency jump comes from the storage compaction tuning change pushed on the evening of 2 Nov, not from gateway 5.8. In 11 cells the change raised compaction threads from 2 to 6. Disks went from 41% to 97% busy within five minutes, and node-side read time rose from 61 to 262 ms. Each cell's latency rose within minutes of its push, whatever gateway version it ran, including cells that still had 5.7 at that moment. One cell (aps-3) skipped the push but runs 5.8, and its latency is unchanged. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 changed nothing. A rollback would also reopen the security hole that must be closed by 30 Nov. Network and traffic growth don't explain it. Next step: revert the compaction change in one cell, watch p99 and backlog, then extend it to the others. Backlog was 11.2% before the change and the projection doesn't reach 15% before 13 Nov, so there is time to do this carefully. Don't pause compaction for weeks. Hold off on pacing Orrin until the 10 Nov attribution report. I'm fairly confident, though the revert test would confirm it.
